optimization_analysis: Merged the two consecutive SEM_FILTER operators into a single operator. The first filter checks only document type (EX-97 clawback), while the second checks three substantive conditions. Combining them eliminates one full-document LM pass. The merged filter applies all four conditions (document type + three substantive requirements) in a single semantic evaluation, reducing LM cost by ~50% on the filtering stage while preserving correctness.

optimized_semantic_plan.program:
SCAN_DOCS(CONTRACTEXHIBIT, all)
-> SEM_FILTER('Keep EX-97 clawback or recoupment policies that treat intentional misconduct as a trigger, extend recovery beyond SEC minimum requirements, and explicitly state an effective date', input_bindings={document: text})
-> SEM_EXTRACT('Return document name, company name, effective date, and concise covered-person scope', out_schema={document_name: string, company_name: string, effective_date: date, covered_persons: string}, input_bindings={document: text})
